Des Moines' Indoor Farmers Markets 2023-24: Complete Winter Shopping Guide

When winter's chill settles over Central Iowa, Des Moines' vibrant farmers market scene doesn't hibernate – it moves indoors! From the historic Valley Junction to the bustling East Village, local vendors continue offering farm-fresh produce, artisanal goods, and warm community connections throughout the cold months.

Winter Farmers Market Locations in Greater Des Moines

Downtown Winter Market

Located in the skywalk system connecting Capital Square and Hy-Vee Hall, the Downtown Winter Market operates on select Fridays and Saturdays from November through April. Over 40 vendors offer locally grown produce, farm-raised meat, artisan cheese, and handcrafted items.

  • Dates: First Friday and Saturday of each month
  • Time: 9am - 1pm
  • Location: Downtown Skywalk System
  • Parking: Available at numerous downtown ramps

Valley Junction Indoor Market

Historic Valley Junction in West Des Moines transforms its charming indoor spaces into a cozy marketplace featuring over 25 local vendors.

  • Dates: Third Thursday of each month
  • Time: 4pm - 8pm
  • Location: 137 5th Street, West Des Moines

What to Find at Des Moines Winter Markets

Local Winter Produce

  • Greenhouse tomatoes and leafy greens
  • Root vegetables and winter squash
  • Microgreens and sprouts
  • Hydroponically grown herbs

Iowa-Made Products

  • Artisanal cheeses from local creameries
  • Fresh-baked goods from Des Moines bakeries
  • Local honey and maple syrup
  • Grass-fed meat from Iowa farms

Tips for Winter Market Shopping

Make the most of your indoor market experience with these local insider tips:

  • Arrive early for the best selection of fresh produce
  • Park in the covered ramps near Capital Square for easy skywalk access
  • Bring reusable bags and cash (though many vendors accept cards)
  • Sign up for vendor newsletters to track seasonal offerings

Supporting Local Agriculture Year-Round

Des Moines' indoor markets play a crucial role in supporting Iowa's agricultural community through the winter months. Many vendors also offer CSA (Community Supported Agriculture) programs, providing a steady supply of local produce even during the coldest days.
